q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a hand pump?
title: Hand pump carbon footprint per pump
short: Weigh the cast iron head, stand, handle, galvanised riser pipes and rods, and cylinder per pump and multiply by supplier figures. Add machining, assembly and painting energy, then divide the workshop's energy by pumps made.
audience: Hand pump makers supplying water schemes

ul: Cast iron or steel head, stand and handle.
Galvanised steel riser pipes and connecting rods.
Brass or plastic cylinder parts and seals.

p: Report per pump by type and depth, since deeper wells need more riser pipe and rod.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per pump (one month)
lines: Plant total: 17,910 / 1,000 = 17.9 kg CO2 per pump
Add iron, pipe and rods for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
